findings.title: Unsanitized feed/remote HTML is stored and rendered as cooked HTML
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true` using content taken directly from external RSS/Readability sources. Post#cook returns `raw` unchanged for raw_html posts, and app/views/embed/best.html.erb renders `raw post.cooked`. A malicious or compromised feed can therefore store `<script>` or event-handler HTML that executes in the Discourse origin (stored XSS). The imported_from footer also interpolates the feed URL into raw HTML without escaping. Imported HTML must be sanitized before storage, or this path must use the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline.

findings.title: Invalid `end if` makes the best embed view fail to compile
findings.body: The template closes the header conditional with `<%- end if %>`. There is no condition after the `if`, so Ruby parses this as an incomplete modifier-if and raises a SyntaxError when the template is compiled. Any successful embed request that finds a `topic_id` and renders `best.html.erb` will fail with a 500. It should be `<%- end %>`.

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses substring matching
findings.body: The listener validates messages with `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`. This accepts any origin that appears as a substring of `discourseUrl`; for example, `http://eviltrout.co` passes when `discourseUrl` is `http://eviltrout.com`. An untrusted window can then send forged `discourse-resize` messages to the embedding page. The origin should be compared exactly against the parsed `discourseUrl` origin.

findings.title: Protocol-relative URLs are corrupted during absolutization
findings.body: The absolutizer treats every href/src beginning with `/` as root-relative. A protocol-relative URL such as `//cdn.example.com/image.png` starts with `/`, so it is rewritten to `http://origin/cdn.example.com/image.png`, breaking links and images in imported feed content. Detect `//` separately and preserve the scheme (or use URI.join).

findings.title: PollFeed assumes every feed item has `content`
findings.body: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` calls `scrub` on `i.content` without checking for nil. Many RSS/Atom feeds expose body text only through `description` (or have empty/missing content), in which case `i.content` is nil and the job raises NoMethodError. Since this job sets `retry: false`, such a feed stops importing items. Guard missing content and fall back to `description` or skip the item.

findings.title: `open(url)` is used without requiring open-uri
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url)` but this file does not require `open-uri`. Only `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` requires it, so when the retrieve-topic job or the Disqus task calls `import_remote` first, Ruby's `Kernel#open` treats the URL as a local filename and raises `Errno::ENOENT`. Add `require 'open-uri'` in this file or in every caller before fetching remote content.

findings.title: Existing migration now drops the top_topics table with `force: true`
findings.body: This PR changes an already-existing migration from `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. If the migration is ever run against a database where `top_topics` exists but the migration is not recorded (for example after a partially failed migration or a restored schema), Rails will drop the table and all of its rows before recreating it. Migrations should be immutable; use a new migration or guard with `unless table_exists?` instead of adding `force: true`.
